statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 conditions remain orderly and two-sided about three hours before the US August employment report at 12:30 UTC.
recommendation: The assessment favours a narrow evidence-based danger window covering the payrolls release and the first hour of US cash trade rather than a session-wide restriction; Tail remains below the block threshold on currently observed evidence, and the CME weekend closure from 21:00 UTC removes live price-path exposure for the remainder of the forecast window.
headline: Payrolls-day drift retraces 42 points from the 29,673.00 overnight high with VIX near 14.2 and oil easing off six-week peaks
body: NQ futures trade at 29,630.75, about +0.36% against a 29,524.75 prior settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,482.00 to 29,673.00 that spans roughly 0.65%. Price sits about 42 points below the overnight high: the last hour extended that high by only about five points and then gave back more than it gained, which is an observed retracement rather than a failed one, and it leaves directional efficiency low. A second independent quote source shows 29,628.50 with the identical 29,673.00 high. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 3 at 29,482.32, up 1.16% in a 29,160.96 to 29,538.76 range, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support holding rates steady if inflation pressures abate; that cut September hike odds to about 50.4% from 63.2% and pulled the 10-year yield toward 4.74% to 4.76% against the 4.79% H.15 print for Sep 2, with the 2-year at 4.39%. VIX at 14.23 is down 0.63% in a 14.13 to 14.23 range. WTI near $90.78 is off 0.57% and Brent near $95.23 off 0.30%, both easing from six-week highs even as Strait of Hormuz transits fell to six vessels from eleven. Sector tone is genuinely mixed rather than aligned: Broadcom's soft fourth-quarter revenue guidance weighs on semiconductors while megacap sentiment stayed firm. The August employment report at 12:30 UTC is the single dominant catalyst, with consensus near +56k after a -23k July decline and unemployment expected at 4.1%; because a rate hike is a live debate, a strong print is the hawkish outcome, so the distribution is genuinely two-sided. Per the standing framework, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and temper Confidence rather than Tail until persistent one-way structure is actually observed, and none is. Tail is therefore held at 16 with Stress at 59. The CME weekend break from 21:00 UTC removes live price-path exposure for the back half of the forecast window.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. The Sep 3 European session was benign with Tail near 13 to 14 and the mode assessed as normal. The mode shifted to trend-up across the US cash session as the Waller-driven rally developed, with Tail peaking at 21 and Stress at 62, then decayed through the US evening as the move matured and the cash index closed up 1.16%. Overnight into Sep 4 the mode returned to normal, Tail held a tight 12 to 16 band and Stress eased into the low 50s before climbing back to 58 as the payrolls report drew closer. No hour in the window produced a persistent no-retracement path, and the highest published Tail stayed below the block threshold throughout.
outlookSummary: The baseline holds a low-amplitude range through the rest of the European session, with Stress building mechanically into the 12:30 UTC August employment report. The release hour and the following digestion hour, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open, carry the widest two-sided repricing risk and are modelled at Tail 20 and 23, which map to WATCH rather than to a block. That is consistent with treating event importance and forecast dispersion as Stress and Confidence inputs until persistent one-way structure is actually observed, and with a genuinely two-sided rate distribution in which a strong print is the hawkish outcome. Tail is modelled to fall back below 20 from 15:00 UTC on the baseline that post-event discovery is orderly, with a modest tick up into the power hour for position-squaring. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend break removes live price discovery entirely, so the final twelve slots carry a floor Tail near 6 to 7; the residual exposure there is weekend gap risk, principally from the Iran conflict, to be priced at the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen beyond this horizon.

VIX at 14.23 and oil easing from six-week highs leave no aligned amplifier, so Tail stays low while Stress carries the approaching 12:30 UTC payrolls print.
